label: IN_ACT_VIRTUALLY_2: A cause is IN_ACT_VIRTUALLY_2, or eminently, in a perfection when it has it in…
definition: A cause is in act virtually, or eminently, in a perfection when it has it in a higher way, as a power to produce it, without having it in the same form: whatever perfection is in the effect is in the effective cause 'univocally or more eminently' (ST I q.4 a.2).
note: Lean: a primitive parameter of the sense-fork frame (its own declaration, distinct from the other senses of its disambiguation); it carries no definitional body.

formal_gap.meaning: ActFrame.InActVirtually x r says that x has the perfection r in a higher way, as a power to produce it, without having it in the same form: whatever perfection is in an effect is in its effective cause 'univocally or more eminently' (ST I q.4 a.2). It is a supplied relation between a being and a respect: the virtual (eminent) sense of 'in act' (DISAMB-IN-ACT).
formal_gap.examples_unavailable: The corpus records no concrete instance: q.4 a.2 states the notion only generally ('univocally or more eminently'), and any instance would need a separate reading of which causes are equivocal.
exclusions: Having r in the same form (InActFormally).
Merely being able to receive r: virtual act is an active power to produce, not a passive capacity.
open_obligations: That nothing is virtually in act and in potency in the same respect is the open premise NothingVirtuallyInActAndInPotency; DISAMB-IN-ACT notes that the Metaphysics IX.6 support for non-simultaneity carries over only on the formal reading.
Its relation to InActFormally and to the shared InAct (DEF-ACT) remains open.
No formalization candidate from existing vocabulary.
